title: U.S. House · Texas's 26th Congressional District
area: North Texas exurbs, including much of Denton County (Denton, Flower Mound, Lewisville).

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional district boundaries in August 2025 ahead of the 2026 elections, a mid-decade redistricting.

In the March 3, 2026 primaries, Brandon Gill defeated Robert Chick 91.1% to 8.9% for the Republican nomination, and Steven Shook defeated Ernest Lineberger III 51.1% to 48.9% for the Democratic nomination. Phil Gray advanced as the Libertarian Party's nominee from its March 21, 2026 convention.

summary.text: Brandon Gill is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Texas's 26th District. A Dartmouth graduate who worked in investment banking and as a hedge fund analyst, he founded the DC Enquirer news outlet before winning the 2024 Republican primary and general election. He serves on the Judiciary, Budget and Oversight committees and is seeking a second term.

background.text: Born in Clovis, New Mexico, in 1994. According to his official biography he was born on a military air force base and raised on a cattle ranch in West Texas; Ballotpedia says he grew up outside Abilene.

Graduated cum laude from Dartmouth College in 2016 with degrees in economics and history. His official biography says he was president of The Dartmouth Review, the student newspaper, and led the Christian Union campus ministry.
Began his career in finance as an investment banker and later as an analyst at a hedge fund, according to his official biography.
Left finance to start the DC Enquirer, which his official biography describes as an America First news outlet; Ballotpedia also lists film producer among his career experience.

Won the March 5, 2024 Republican primary for the open 26th District seat with 58.4% of the vote in a field of more than ten candidates, then won the November 2024 general election with 62.1%, defeating Democrat Ernest Lineberger III and Libertarian Phil Gray.

Took office January 3, 2025. Ballotpedia lists his 2025–2026 committee assignments as Oversight and Government Reform, Judiciary and Budget; his official biography says he serves on Judiciary, Budget and Oversight, including the DOGE Subcommittee.
Advanced from the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, in which he defeated Robert Chick, and is on the November ballot for a second term.
According to his official biography, he is married to Danielle D'Souza Gill, an author, and they live in Flower Mound, Texas, with their two children.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, the House Committee on the Judiciary, and the House Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Steven Shook
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 51.1% of the vote

summary.text: Steven Shook is a nurse practitioner who says he has spent nearly two decades caring for critically ill and injured patients in North Texas. He won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary and describes his priorities as keeping rural hospitals open, lowering healthcare costs, supporting local businesses and restoring accountability in Washington.

background.text: Born in Arlington, Texas, and graduated from Keys High School, according to Ballotpedia.
Earned an associate degree from Tarrant County College in 2009, a bachelor's degree from Texas Tech University in 2012 and a graduate degree from the University of Texas at Arlington in 2018.
Has worked as a nurse practitioner; in his Candidate Connection survey he says he has served North Texas as a healthcare provider for nearly twenty years, caring for the critically ill and injured.
Defeated Ernest Lineberger III, the 2024 Democratic nominee, in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, 51.1% to 48.9%.
In his survey he lists his priorities as keeping rural hospitals open, lowering healthcare costs, supporting local businesses and job growth, community policing and government accountability.

priorities.text: In his Ballotpedia survey, listed his priorities as keeping rural hospitals open, lowering healthcare costs, supporting local businesses and job growth, strengthening public safety through community policing, and restoring accountability in Washington.

positions.summary: Says every American deserves affordable, reliable healthcare and that rural hospitals must be kept open.
Says he would strengthen public safety through community policing and support local law enforcement.

candidates.name: Phil Gray
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced as the Libertarian Party's nominee from its March 21, 2026 state convention

summary.text: Phil Gray is the Libertarian Party nominee for Texas's 26th District, a repeat candidate who has appeared on Texas congressional ballots in several districts since 2016. Ballotpedia lists his career experience as business owner and property manager. His campaign materials emphasize reducing the national debt, immigration reform, drug decriminalization and healthcare price transparency.

background.text: Career experience includes owning a business and working as a property manager; has been affiliated with AARP, LULAC and the Urban League, according to Ballotpedia.
Ballotpedia lists earlier Libertarian candidacies for Texas's 1st District (2016), 27th District (2020), 30th District (2022) and 26th District (2024).
In 2024 he received 2.3% (8,773 votes) in the general election for this seat, won by Brandon Gill. Advanced from the Libertarian convention on March 21, 2026, for this year's race.

His 2024 campaign website, as reproduced by Ballotpedia, stated a goal of national debt reduction, immigration reform that lets undocumented immigrants voluntarily pay toward the national debt, decriminalizing drug use, and healthcare price transparency.

priorities.text: His campaign website centers on reducing the national debt, including a proposal to let immigrants pay to expedite entry with the funds used to pay down debt and fund low-interest loans in place of some tax-funded programs.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in Texas, 2026

researchNotes: Gill's positions are limited to official committee assignments; no 2026 Candidate Connection survey or campaign-site statements were found for him at research time. Shook completed his Candidate Connection survey in 2025, before the 2026 cycle. Phil Gray has not completed a 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his positions are drawn from his campaign website as reproduced by Ballotpedia. Federal key votes and FEC totals for the incumbent are added separately by script. Little biographical information on Phil Gray exists beyond his Ballotpedia profile (career, affiliations and election history); no personal background, education or news profile was found.
